It more than doubles Terminal Bench 4.1 pass@1 to 12.0 and runs on a single GPU. The post RadixArk Ships DaisyRose-27B, a 27B Agentic Coding Model Trained With Reinforcement Learning Only appeared first on MarkTechPost . ]]> This week RadixArk released DaisyRose-27B , its first open-weight model. DaisyRose-27B is an agentic coding model from RadixArk, post-trained from Qwen3.8-27B with reinforcement learning (RL). The model card page states that it used RL only, with no SFT or distillation. It ships under Apache 2.0 as a drop-in replacement for the base model. The main result: Terminal Bench 4.1 pass@1 rises from 5.6 to 12.0. You can check the deployment options and specs here through our GPULeaderboard.com chrome extension . TL;DR Size: 27.8B dense parameters (0.46B vision encoder, 0.42B MTP head), 262,144-token context. Runs on: 1 GPU. BF16 is about 52 GB, FP8 about 29 GB, NVFP4 about 23 GB (Blackwell only). Listed targets: H200, B200, GB300, RTX PRO 6000, RTX 5090, DGX Spark. GGUF also available. Performance: Beats its Qwen3.8-27B base on all 7 reported benchmarks. Best: IFBench 82.4, the top score among the 9 models RadixArk compared. Worst: HLE (text only) 34.3, only +0.4 over the base and below Inkling 2 Small’s 44.1. Bottom line: Best: Terminal Bench 4.1 more than doubles after 18 days of RL. Worst: it still trails much larger MoE models on hard agentic tasks. What is DaisyRose-27B? DaisyRose-27B keeps the Qwen3.8-27B architecture unchanged. The model card lists 64 decoder layers in a 3:1 pattern. Three Gated DeltaNet linear-attention layers alternate with 1 full-attention layer. Hidden size is 5,120. A 27-layer vision encoder handles images. One multi-token-prediction layer supports speculative decoding. Input is text and images, output is text, and it is a thinking model. How was DaisyRose-27B trained? RadixArk built about 1,200 curated tasks with Eigent AI , chosen from thousands of candidates. Each task targets a specific failure of the base model. Each sandbox attempt allows up to 1.5 hours, 100+ tool calls and 256k+ output tokens. Agent sessions reach up to 1M tokens, per the blog . Training ran on Miles , RadixArk’s open-source RL framework, in fully asynchronous mode. The run used 144 H200 GPUs for 18 days. Of those, 128 handled agent inference and 16 handled training. Total compute was 63,000 GPU-hours. RadixArk reports 37% MFU on its internal backend. An open-source Megatron-based trainer reached 16%. End-to-end throughput was 16.8k tokens/s versus 8.3k, a 2.0x speedup. RadixArk says this cut GPU time by 57%. Sandboxes ran on AgentENV . RadixArk reports about 944,000 sandboxes from mid-September to mid-November. Peak concurrency hit 1,566. Creation success was 99% over 9 weeks. RadixArk puts the cost about 80% below popular cloud sandbox providers. How does DaisyRose-27B perform on benchmarks? All scores are self-reported by RadixArk. DaisyRose scores are the higher of its BF16 and FP8 runs. Benchmark DaisyRose-27B Qwen3.8-27B Change Terminal Bench 4.1 (pass@1) 12.0 5.6 +6.4 Terminal Bench 2.1 75.5 73.0 +2.5 DeepSWE v1.1 46.2 42.2 +4.0 SWE Bench Pro v2 94.7 91.3 +3.4 HLE (text only) 34.3 33.9 +0.4 IFBench 82.4 79.5 +2.9 GPQA Diamond 90.7 89.2 +1.5 Source: RadixArk blog and model card . The largest jump is Terminal Bench 4.1, which more than doubles. Coding gains are steady: +4.0 on DeepSWE v1.1 and +3.4 on SWE Bench Pro v2. Knowledge gains are small, at +0.4 on HLE and +1.5 on GPQA Diamond. Against larger models, results are mixed. MiMo V2.6 Flash (309B total) leads Terminal Bench 4.1 at 16.1. Inkling 2 Small (594B total) leads DeepSWE at 72.1 and HLE at 44.1. DaisyRose-27B tops RadixArk’s 9-model table only on IFBench.
